$comment: The room's packs. grant human: only the person may let a blocked command run.

room-file-write.reason: a write into the room's own files or an agent's settings
room-file-write.explanation: The room's home, each seat's runtime, the agents' settings and the global git config decide what every seat may do and what runs on each git command; a seat changes none of them.
safer: Ask your Owner; the person changes these

git-global-config.reason: git config --global or --system changes git for every repository
git-global-config.explanation: Global git config holds aliases, hooks paths and credential helpers that run on every git command anywhere on the machine.
safer: git config --local inside this repository

guard-off.reason: an attempt to turn off or route around the room's command guard
guard-off.explanation: An agent started from a seat's shell runs without the room's hooks, so whatever it does is never checked.
safer: Ask your Owner for another seat

git-config-write.reason: a write into .git where git reads programs from: config, hooks or attributes
git-config-write.explanation: A filter, hook or external diff named in these files runs on the room's own git calls too, outside the guard.
safer: Ask your Owner; the person changes a repository's git configuration

git-config-exec.reason: git config names a program git runs later: a filter, a text conversion, an external diff, a hook path
git-config-exec.explanation: What the repository's config names runs on every git call there, the room's own included, outside the guard.
safer: Ask your Owner; the person changes a repository's git configuration

git-no-verify.reason: git told to skip the repository's hooks
git-no-verify.explanation: The hooks are the project's own checks on a commit or push; work that skips them goes in unchecked.
safer: Run the hooks and fix what they report
If a hook itself is broken, tell your Owner with its output

git-attributes-driver.reason: a .gitattributes line that names a filter or driver of the repository's own
git-attributes-driver.explanation: git runs the program the repository's config gives such a name, on every git call there, the room's own included, outside the guard.
safer: Ask your Owner; the person changes how a repository's files are converted

paseo-cli.reason: a seat reaching other agents or the daemon through the Paseo CLI
paseo-cli.explanation: The Paseo CLI sends prompts to agents, starts, stops and schedules them, answers their permission requests and changes the daemon. What it sends arrives as if the person wrote it, and none of the room's checks stand between.
safer: seatwork_mail writes to your Owner or to a seat you launched
Ask your Owner; the person runs the Paseo CLI

paseo-daemon.reason: a seat reaching the Paseo daemon by its address or its client library
paseo-daemon.explanation: The daemon takes a program on this machine for its owner: what it is sent prompts, starts and stops agents and changes the daemon, and none of the room's checks stand between.
safer: seatwork_mail writes to your Owner or to a seat you launched
Ask your Owner; the person works with the daemon

brew-install.reason: brew puts software on the machine
brew-install.explanation: Installing, upgrading or tapping with Homebrew changes the machine for every project; the person decides what is installed.
safer: Use what is already installed
Ask your Owner to ask the person

global-package.reason: a global package install changes the machine, not the project
global-package.explanation: npm -g, pnpm -g, yarn global and bun -g write outside the project and change commands every project sees.
safer: Install into the project (npm install --save-dev <pkg>)
Run it once with npx

tool-install.reason: a tool installer puts programs on the machine
tool-install.explanation: pipx, uv tool, cargo install, go install and gem install put programs on the user's PATH.
safer: uvx <tool> or npx <tool> runs it once without installing
Ask your Owner

runtime-install.reason: a version manager downloads a runtime or toolchain
runtime-install.explanation: nvm, fnm, volta, pyenv, rbenv, rustup, asdf, mise and sdkman download whole runtimes onto the machine.
safer: Use the runtime already installed
Ask your Owner

browser-install.explanation: Browser downloads are large and land on the machine; the person chose which browser the room may use.
safer: Use the browser already installed
Ask your Owner

system-package.reason: a system package manager installs software
system-package.explanation: apt, yum, dnf, apk, pacman, port, mas and installer change the operating system.
safer: Ask your Owner

download-and-run.reason: a download piped straight into a shell or interpreter
download-and-run.explanation: The downloaded text runs before anyone reads it; it can install or change anything the user can.
safer: Download to a file, read it, then ask your Owner
